newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka cuts statutory reserve to boost growth.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka cuts statutory reserve to boost growth.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Central Bank said on Monday it had cut the statutory reserve that commercial banks must hold against deposits of local and foreign currencies.

"The statutory reserves which commercial banks have to hold with the Central Bank as a percentage of their deposit liabilities has been reduced from 15 to 14 percent," the central bank said in a statement.
The bank said it had also eliminated the five percent statutory reserve requirement on foreign currency deposits placed abroad.

Along with permission granted last week to exporters to borrow in foreign currencies, the measures were expected to increase the lending capacity of commercial banks by about 10 billion rupees or five percent, the Central Bank said.
It said it considered an easing in monetary policy helpful in giving an impetus to economic growth without causing inflationary pressure.
The economy, which suffered in 1996 from a drought and power cuts, was showing signs of recovery, the Central Bank added.
The Central Bank is expected this week to announce when the new regulation would come into effect.
